results.title: Morley's categoricity theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language with at most countably many symbols, and let $T$ be a complete $L$-theory all of whose models are infinite. Call $T$ $\kappa$-categorical if any two models of $T$ of cardinality $\kappa$ are isomorphic. If $T$ is $\kappa$-categorical for some uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, then $T$ is $\mu$-categorical for every uncountable cardinal $\mu$.

results.title: Extremal points of the Josephus function near $2k - 2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $J_k$ be the Josephus function; call $m$ low extremal if $1 \le J_k(m) \le k - 1$, and high extremal if $m + 1$ is low extremal. If $J_k(2k - 2) \le k - 1$, then $2k - 3$ is high extremal and $2k - 2$ is low extremal. If $J_k(2k - 2) > k - 1$, then $2k - 2$ is high extremal and $2k - 1$ is low extremal. In particular, $2k - 2$ is always a low or a high extremal point.

results.title: Linear-step bound at a low extremal point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $J_k$ be the Josephus function, write $j = J_k(n+1)$, and suppose $j \le k - 1$. Then for every natural number $m$, $j + km \le n + 1 + m$ holds if and only if $m \le \lfloor (n - (j - 1)) / (k - 1) \rfloor$. Moreover, if $k - 2 + j \le n$, then $\lfloor (n - (j - 1)) / (k - 1) \rfloor \ge 1$.

results.title: Linear growth of the Josephus function after a high extremal point

Then $J_k(n_e + 1 + m) = j + km$ for every natural number $m \le \lfloor (n_e - (j - 1)) / (k - 1) \rfloor$.

results.title: Overlap count of two finite sets of integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and an integer $k$, the overlap of $A$ and $B$ at $k$ is the number of pairs $(a, b) \in A \times B$ with $a - b = k$.

results.title: Maximum overlap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$ is the natural number obtained as the supremum over all integers $k$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$.

results.title: Erdős minimum overlap function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $M(n)$ is the least value of the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$, the supremum over $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$, taken over all pairs of disjoint finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $A \cup B = \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ and $|A| = |B|$.

results.title: Overlaps are bounded by the maximum overlap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and every integer $k$, the overlap $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$ is at most the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$.

results.title: The maximum overlap is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ there is an integer $k$ such that the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$, the supremum over $j \in \mathbb{Z}$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = j\}$, equals $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$.

results.title: Balanced partitions of $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$ exist

results.summary: For an admissible pair $(f, g)$ let $S(f, g)$ be its pair score, the supremum over $x \in [-2, 2]$ of $\int_{-1}^{1} f(t)\,g(x + t)\,dt$. The continuous minimum-overlap constant $C_{1b}$ is the supremum of the set of real numbers $c$ such that $c \le S(f, g)$ for every admissible pair $(f, g)$.

results.title: Borsuk covers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s$ be a set in an extended pseudometric space and let $k$ be a natural number. The set $s$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover if there are $k$ sets whose union contains $s$, each of extended diameter strictly smaller than that of $s$.

results.title: Borsuk number of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Borsuk number of a set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the least natural number $k$ such that $s$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover, that is, $s$ is covered by $k$ sets each of strictly smaller extended diameter than $s$; it is $\infty$ if no such $k$ exists.

results.title: Borsuk number of a Euclidean space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Borsuk number of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is the supremum, in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, of the Borsuk numbers of the bounded subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with at least two points.

results.title: First Borsuk failure dimension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The first Borsuk failure dimension is the least positive integer $n$ such that the Borsuk number of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is greater than $n + 1$, and $\infty$ if there is no such $n$.

results.title: A Borsuk cover bounds the Borsuk number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover for a natural number $k$, then the Borsuk number of $s$ is at most $k$.

results.title: Borsuk covers by subsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, a set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover if and only if there are subsets $c_1, \dots, c_k$ of $s$ with $s = c_1 \cup \dots \cup c_k$, each of extended diameter strictly smaller than that of $s$.

results.title: Borsuk covers by closed sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, a set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover if and only if there are $k$ closed subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose union contains $s$, each of extended diameter strictly smaller than that of $s$.

results.title: Borsuk covers of nonempty sets have at least one piece
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. If a nonempty set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover, then $0 < k$.

results.title: Enlarging a Borsuk cover
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $l$ be natural numbers with $k \le l$. If a nonempty set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover, then $s$ has an $l$-piece Borsuk cover.

results.title: Bounds on the Borsuk number of a set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a nonempty set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and a natural number $k$, the Borsuk number of $s$ is at most $k$ if and only if $s$ has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover.

results.title: Upper bounds on the Borsuk number of a Euclidean space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the Borsuk number of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is at most $k$ if and only if every bounded subset $s$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with at least two points has a $k$-piece Borsuk cover, that is, $s$ is covered by $k$ sets, each of extended diameter strictly smaller than that of $s$.

results.title: Borsuk's conjecture in a given dimension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, Borsuk's conjecture in dimension $n$ is the statement that the Borsuk number of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is at most $n + 1$.

results.title: When the first Borsuk failure dimension is infinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The first Borsuk failure dimension is $\infty$ if and only if, for every positive integer $n$, the Borsuk number of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is at most $n + 1$.

results.title: Two-distance sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $s$ in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a two-distance set if there are reals $0 < a < b$ such that the distance between any two distinct points of $s$ is $a$ or $b$, and both $a$ and $b$ occur as the distance between some two points of $s$.

results.title: Two-distance Borsuk number in dimension $n$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The two-distance Borsuk number in dimension $n$ is the supremum, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, of the Borsuk numbers of all bounded two-distance sets with at least two points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$.

results.title: Dart diagram
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A dart diagram consists of a finite set $V$ of crossings, a fixed-point-free involution $\mathrm{pair}$ of the set $V \times \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ of darts, and a natural number counting isolated crossingless components.

results.title: Darts of a dart diagram
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The darts of a dart diagram $D$ with crossing set $V$ are the pairs $(v, i)$ with $v \in V$ and $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$; the dart $(v, i)$ is the $i$-th incident half-edge at the crossing $v$.

results.title: Number of crossings of a dart diagram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The crossing count of a dart diagram $D$ is the number of vertices of $D$, each vertex being one crossing.

results.title: Rotation of a dart
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation of a dart $(v, i)$ of $D$, with $v$ a crossing and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, is the dart $(v, i + 1)$: one step counterclockwise around the crossing $v$.

results.title: Opposite dart
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d = (v, i)$ of $D$, the opposite dart is obtained by rotating $d$ twice counterclockwise around its crossing $v$; it is the dart $(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.

results.title: Over-strand darts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The four darts at a crossing of a dart diagram carry the labels $0, 1, 2, 3$ in cyclic order. A dart lies on the over-strand at its crossing when its label is $0$ or $2$.

results.title: Edge-pairing permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the edge-pairing permutation is the edge-pairing involution of $D$ regarded as a permutation of the darts of $D$; it is its own inverse.

results.title: Rotation permutation of darts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation permutation is the permutation of the darts of $D$ sending a dart $(v, i)$, with $v$ a crossing and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, to $(v, i + 1)$; its inverse sends $(v, i)$ to $(v, i - 1)$.

results.title: Opposite-dart permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the opposite-dart permutation of the darts of $D$ is the square of the quarter-turn rotation permutation: it sends the dart $(v, i)$ at crossing $v$ to the dart $(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.

results.title: Strand traversal step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d$ of $D$, the next dart after $d$ is the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where $\mathrm{pair}$ is the edge-pairing involution of $D$: cross the edge segment at $d$, then go straight through the crossing reached.

results.title: Strand traversal permutation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the strand traversal permutation of the darts of $D$ is the edge-pairing permutation followed by the opposite-dart permutation: it sends a dart $d$ to the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where $\mathrm{pair}$ is the edge-pairing involution of $D$.

results.title: A traversal step stays in its strand cycle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be a dart diagram, and for a dart $d$ of $D$ let $\operatorname{next}(d)$ be the dart reached from $d$ by crossing its edge segment and then going straight through the next crossing. Then for every dart $d$ of $D$, the darts $d$ and $\operatorname{next}(d)$ lie in the same cycle of the strand traversal permutation of $D$, the permutation of the darts of $D$ that sends each dart $e$ to…

results.title: Alternating dart diagrams
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A dart diagram is alternating when, for every dart $d$, the dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$, reached from $d$ by crossing its edge segment and going straight through the next crossing, has the opposite over/under status to $d$. In other words, consecutive crossings on every strand have opposite over/under status.

results.title: Same component relation on darts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, two darts of $D$ lie in the same component when they are related by the equivalence relation on darts generated by $d \sim \operatorname{pair}(d)$, crossing an edge segment, and $d \sim \operatorname{opposite}(d)$, going straight through a crossing.

results.title: Strand-connectivity relation on darts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, this is the equivalence relation on the darts of $D$ generated by relating each dart $d$ to its partner across an edge segment and to the opposite dart of $d$ at the same crossing. Two darts are related exactly when they lie on the same unoriented strand component.

results.title: A traversal step stays in the same component
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every dart $d$ of a dart diagram $D$, the dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$ reached by one step of strand traversal lies in the same component as $d$.

results.title: Number of components of a dart diagram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of components of a dart diagram $D$ is the number of classes of darts of $D$ under unoriented strand connectivity, plus the recorded number of isolated crossingless components of $D$.

results.title: Isolated components are counted in the component count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every dart diagram $D$, the number of isolated crossingless components recorded in $D$ is at most the number of components of $D$.

results.title: Empty dart diagram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, the empty dart diagram with $k$ isolated components has no crossings, hence no darts, and records $k$ isolated crossingless components.

results.title: Euclidean plane
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm, the target plane of the fixed standard projection frame.

results.title: Standard projection to the plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The standard projection sends a point $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2)$ of Euclidean 3-space to the point $(x_0, x_1)$ of the Euclidean plane, forgetting the third coordinate.

results.title: Height in the standard projection frame
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The height of a point $x = (x_1, x_2, x_3)$ of Euclidean 3-space is its third coordinate $x_3$.

results.title: Parameter point
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, a parameter point consists of a component index $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a real parameter $t$ with $0 \le t < 2\pi$, the fundamental half-open period. It represents the point at parameter $t$ of component $i$ of a parametrized link with $n$ components.

results.title: Point of a link at a parameter point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point $a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the point of $L$ at $a$ is $\gamma_i(t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$.

results.title: Projected curve of a link component
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and $i < n$, the projected curve of component $i$ is the map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^2$, $t \mapsto \pi(\gamma_i(t))$, where $\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ is the standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.

results.title: Projected point of a link at a parameter point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point $a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the projected point of $L$ at $a$ is $\pi(\gamma_i(t)) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, where $\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ forgets the third coordinate.

results.title: Projected tangent vector
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and let $a$ be a parameter point of $L$, given by a component $i$ and a parameter $t$. The projected tangent vector of $L$ at $a$ is the vector of $\mathbb{R}^2$ obtained by applying the standard projection $(x, y, z) \mapsto (x, y)$ to the derivative $\gamma_i'(t)$ of the curve $\gamma_i$ of the $i$-th component of $L$ at $t$.

results.title: Height of a parameter point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components and a parameter point $a$ of $L$, the height of $L$ at $a$ is the height (the third coordinate) of the point of Euclidean 3-space that $a$ represents on $L$.

results.title: Double points of a link projection
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the double-point set of $L$ is the set of points $p$ of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ for which there are two distinct parameter points of $L$ (each a component index together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) whose images under the standard projection, which forgets the third coordinate, both equal $p$.

results.title: Regular projections
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link; a parameter point of $L$ is a component of $L$ together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$. The standard projection of $L$ to the plane, which forgets the third coordinate, is regular when the following hold: at every parameter point, the projection of the velocity vector of the component curve is nonzero; the double-point set is finite; no three pairwise distinct parameter points have…

results.title: Points with the same projection have different heights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components. If two distinct parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ have the same projected point, then the heights of $L$ at $a$ and at $b$ are different.

results.title: Crossings of a link projection
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components. A crossing of $L$ is a point of the double-point set of $L$, that is, a point $p$ of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that two distinct parameter points of $L$ both have image $p$ under the standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.

results.title: Crossing count of a regular projection
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ whose standard projection is regular, the crossing count of $L$ is the number of crossings of the projection, that is, the number of points of its double-point set.

results.title: Double points have exactly two preimages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a point of the double-point set of $L$. Then there are parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ whose projected points are both $p$, and every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is $a$ or $b$.

results.title: Being the over-strand preimage of a crossing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an over point of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly smaller height than $a$.

results.title: Being the under-strand preimage of a crossing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an under point of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly greater height than $a$.

results.title: The over-strand preimage exists and is unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an over-strand preimage of $p$: the projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has height strictly less than the height of $a$.

results.title: The under-strand preimage exists and is unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an under-strand preimage of $p$: the projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has height strictly greater than the height of $a$.

results.title: Over-strand preimage of a crossing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. The over-strand preimage of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and such that every other parameter point projecting to $p$ has strictly smaller height than $a$.

results.title: Under-strand preimage of a crossing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. The under-strand preimage of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and whose height is strictly less than the height of every other parameter point projecting to $p$; the height of a parameter point is the third coordinate of the corresponding point of $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

results.title: Over and under preimages differ
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. Then the under-strand preimage of $p$ and the over-strand preimage of $p$ are distinct parameter points of $L$.

results.title: The under-strand lies strictly below the over-strand
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. The height of $L$ at the under-strand preimage of $p$ is strictly less than its height at the over-strand preimage of $p$.

results.title: The over-strand preimage lies over its crossing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the over-strand parameter point at $p$ is $p$.

results.title: The under-strand preimage lies over its crossing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the under-strand parameter point at $p$ is $p$.

results.title: The over and under preimages exhaust a crossing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. Every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is either the over-strand preimage or the under-strand preimage of $p$.

results.title: A crossing-free regular projection has crossing count zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then the crossing count of $L$ is $0$.

results.title: A regular projection with a crossing has positive crossing count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection with at least one crossing, then the crossing count of $L$ is positive.

results.title: Crossing number of a link
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the crossing number of $L$ is the infimum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, over all parametrized links $L'$ with $n$ components that are ambient isotopic to $L$ and whose standard projection to the plane is regular, of the number of crossings (double points) of that projection of $L'$. It is $\infty$ when no such $L'$ exists.

results.title: Regular projections of isotopic links bound the crossing number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be oriented labeled parametrized links with $n$ components, with $L'$ ambient isotopic to $L$, and suppose the standard projection of $L'$ to the plane is regular. Then the crossing number of $L$ is at most the number of crossings of this projection of $L'$.

results.title: A link's own regular projection bounds its crossing number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the standard projection of an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ to the plane is regular, then the crossing number of $L$ is at most the number of crossings of this projection.

results.title: Finiteness of the crossing number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be oriented labeled parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L'$ is ambient isotopic to $L$ and the standard projection of $L'$ to the plane is regular, then the crossing number of $L$ is finite.

results.title: The crossing number is an isotopy invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two parametrized links $L_1$ and $L_2$ with $n$ components are isotopic, then $L_1$ and $L_2$ have the same crossing number.

results.title: Crossing number zero from a crossing-free representative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be parametrized links with $n$ components such that $L'$ is isotopic to $L$. If the standard projection of $L'$ is regular and its double-point set is empty, then the crossing number of $L$ is $0$.

results.title: Crossing preimages
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A parameter point $a$ of a parametrized link $L$ (a component of $L$ together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) is a crossing preimage when its image under the standard projection to the plane lies in the double-point set of $L$.

results.title: Over/under status at a crossing preimage
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular, and let $a$ be a crossing preimage of $L$. The over/under status at $a$ is true when $a$ is the over-strand preimage of the crossing at the projection of $a$, that is, the preimage of that crossing of greatest height, and false otherwise.

results.title: The two preimages of a crossing have opposite status
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. If $a \ne b$ are crossing preimages of $L$ with the same projection, then the over/under status at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.

results.title: Open arc on the parameter circle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be parameter points with parameters $s$, $u$, $t \in [0, 2\pi)$ respectively. Then $c$ lies in the open counterclockwise arc from $a$ to $b$ when $s < t < u$ in case $s < u$, and when $s < t$ or $t < u$ in case $u \le s$. Only the parameters are compared; the components of $a$, $b$, $c$ play no role.

results.title: Cyclically adjacent crossing preimages

results.summary: Let $L$ be an oriented labeled parametrized link, with each component parametrized by $t \in [0, 2\pi)$. Two distinct parameter points $a$ and $b$ of $L$ on the same component are cyclically adjacent, in this order, when both are crossing preimages (they project to double points of the standard projection) and no crossing preimage on that component lies in the open arc from $a$ to $b$ in the direction of increasing…

results.title: Alternating regular projections
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. The projection is alternating when, for any two cyclically adjacent crossing preimages $a$ and $b$ of $L$ (distinct, on the same component, with no other crossing preimage of that component in the open arc of parameters from $a$ to $b$), the over/under status at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.

results.title: Crossingless regular projections are alternating
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. If the double-point set of this projection is empty, then the projection is alternating.

results.title: Links admitting an alternating diagram
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components admits an alternating diagram when there is a parametrized link $L'$ isotopic to $L$ whose standard projection is regular and alternating.

results.title: Admitting an alternating diagram is an isotopy invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L_1$ is isotopic to $L_2$ and $L_1$ admits an alternating diagram, then $L_2$ admits an alternating diagram.

results.title: Links with a crossing-free regular projection admit alternating diagrams
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then $L$ admits an alternating diagram.

results.title: The projected trace is the union of the projected components
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the union over all components $i$ of the images of the projected curves of $L$ equals the image of the trace of $L$ under the standard projection to the plane.

results.title: Instances of ACHROMATIC NUMBER

results.title: Well-formed ACHROMATIC NUMBER instances

results.title: Hamiltonian paths
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a list of pairs of natural numbers, viewed as the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ whose arcs are the pairs in $E$ with both ends below $n$. A list $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ when it lists each of the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$ exactly once, starts at $s$, ends at $t$, and each two consecutive entries of $p$ form an arc.

results.title: The HAMPATH problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem that accepts a bit string $x$ exactly when, for some $s$, $t$, $n$ and list of pairs $E$, $x$ is the PATH encoding of $s$, $t$ and the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ with edge list $E$, and this digraph has a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$.

results.title: Distinct variables of a formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The list of the distinct variables of a CNF formula $\varphi$, in order of occurrence in $\varphi$, with each variable kept at its last occurrence.

results.title: Tops of the diamonds
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, the top of diamond $i$ is the vertex $m + i(3m + 2)$; it is also the bottom of diamond $i - 1$.

results.title: Row vertices of a diamond
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, write $T(i)$ for the top of diamond $i$. Row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$ is the number $T(i) + 1 + l$; the row of diamond $i$ consists of the vertices with $l \le 3m$.

results.title: Arcs of a variable diamond

results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses, and write $T(i)$ for the top of diamond $i$ and $R(i, l)$ for its row vertex $l$. The arcs of diamond $i$ for variable $x$ are $T(i) \to R(i, 0)$, $T(i) \to R(i, 3m)$, $R(i, 0) \to T(i + 1)$ and $R(i, 3m) \to T(i + 1)$; for every $l < 3m$, both $R(i, l) \to R(i, l + 1)$ and $R(i, l + 1) \to R(i, l)$; and for every clause $j < m$, the arcs $R(i, 3j + 1) \to j$ and…

results.title: Arcs of the HAMPATH construction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ be its distinct variables, in the order of the distinct-variable list of $\varphi$. The arcs of the construction for $\varphi$ are the arcs of diamond $i$ for variable $x_i$, for $i = 0, \dots, k - 1$, concatenated in this order.

results.title: Sipser's HAMPATH instance of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition

Put $T_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ and $R_{i,l} = T_i + 1 + l$. The result is the encoded PATH instance with vertices $0, \dots, T_k$, source $T_0$, target $T_k$, and, for…

results.title: A fixed HAMPATH no-instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The encoded PATH instance on the two vertices $0$ and $1$, with no arcs, whose source and target are both $0$.

results.title: The SAT-to-HAMPATH reduction map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A bit string $x$ that decodes to a CNF formula $\varphi$ is sent to Sipser's HAMPATH instance of $\varphi$, and a bit string that does not decode to a CNF formula is sent to the fixed HAMPATH no-instance (two vertices, no arcs, source and target $0$).

results.title: Normal clause detours
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses and $k$ distinct variables, and write $R(i, l)$ for row vertex $l$ of diamond $i$ in the HAMPATH construction for $\varphi$. A list of vertices $p$ has normal detours when for every clause $j < m$ there is a diamond $i < k$ such that $p$ contains $R(i, 3j + 1), j, R(i, 3j + 2)$ or $R(i, 3j + 2), j, R(i, 3j + 1)$ as consecutive entries.

results.title: Tops are monotone in the diamond index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the HAMPATH construction with $m$ clauses, if $i \le i'$ then the top of diamond $i$ is at most the top of diamond $i'$.

results.title: Row vertices lie below the next top

results.title: Bits of an edge list, first edge first
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $u, v$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the bit encoding of the edge list whose first edge is $(u, v)$ and whose remaining edges are $E$ is: $u$ copies of true, then false, then $v$ copies of true, then false, then the bit encoding of $E$.

results.title: Edge bits of the empty edge list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The edge-list bit encoding of the empty list of edges is the empty bit string.

results.title: Bits of concatenated edge lists
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all lists $E$ and $E'$ of pairs of natural numbers, the bit encoding of the concatenation of $E$ and $E'$ is the bit encoding of $E$ followed by the bit encoding of $E'$.

results.title: Witness encoding
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The witness encoding of a list $p$ of natural numbers (the vertices of a candidate path) is the bit string obtained by writing each entry $v$ of $p$, in order, as $v$ copies of true followed by one false, and concatenating the results.

results.title: Witness decoder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The witness decoder reads a list $w$ of bits as a list of natural numbers. On the empty list it returns the empty list. Otherwise it reads a unary number $v$ from the front of $w$, a run of $v$ copies of true ended by false, and if decoding the remaining bits gives a list $p$, it returns $v$ followed by $p$. It fails if no unary number can be read from a nonempty list, or if decoding the remaining bits fails.

results.title: Witness encoding of the empty list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The witness encoding of the empty list of vertices is the empty bit string.

results.title: Witness encoding of a nonempty list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a natural number $v$ and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of the list with first entry $v$ followed by $p$ is the bit string made of $v$ copies of true, then one false, then the witness encoding of $p$.

results.title: The witness encoding respects concatenation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For lists $p$ and $p'$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of the concatenation of $p$ and $p'$ is the witness encoding of $p$ followed by the witness encoding of $p'$.

results.title: Decoding the empty witness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The witness decoder succeeds on the empty list of bits and returns the empty list of vertices.

results.title: Witness decoding fails on a cut-off first number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a list $w$ of bits is nonempty and reading a unary number (a run of true ended by false) from the front of $w$ fails, that is, every bit of $w$ is true, then the witness decoder fails on $w$.

results.title: Decoding peels off the first number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If reading a unary number from the front of a list $w$ of bits returns $v$ with remaining bits $r$, that is, $w$ is $v$ copies of true, then false, then $r$, then the witness decoder succeeds on $w$ exactly when it succeeds on $r$, and its result on $w$ is $v$ followed by its result on $r$.

results.title: Decoding inverts the witness encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness decoder applied to the witness encoding of $p$ (each entry $v$ written as $v$ copies of true followed by false) succeeds and returns $p$.

results.title: The witness decoder succeeds only on encodings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit string $w$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers, if the witness decoder returns $p$ on $w$, then $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$.

results.title: The witness codec
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $w$ of bits and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness decoder returns $p$ on $w$ if and only if $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$, which writes each entry $v$ of $p$ as $v$ copies of true followed by false.

results.title: Witness length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $p = (v_1, \dots, v_k)$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of $p$ has length $\sum_{i=1}^{k} (v_i + 1)$.

results.title: Witness length bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers all below $n$, the witness encoding of $p$ has length at most $|p| \cdot n$.

results.title: A witness is at least as long as its vertex list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $p$ of natural numbers, the witness encoding of $p$ has length at least $|p|$.

results.title: Arc check of a vertex list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers, the arc check of a list $p$ of natural numbers returns true when every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ satisfy $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$, and false otherwise; in particular every list with fewer than two entries passes.

results.title: Checking a vertex list against the arcs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every list $E$ of pairs of natural numbers and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the arc check of $p$ against $n$ and $E$ returns true if and only if every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ form an arc of the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ listed by $E$, that is, $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$.

results.title: The Hamiltonian path check
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a natural number $n$, an edge list $E$, vertices $s$ and $t$ and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the Boolean test that $p$ has no repeated entries, has length $n$, has all entries below $n$, has first entry $s$ and last entry $t$, and that every two consecutive entries $u, v$ of $p$ satisfy $(u, v) \in E$, $u < n$ and $v < n$.

results.title: The Hamiltonian path check is correct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$, $s$, $t$, every edge list $E$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the Hamiltonian path check on $(n, E, s, t, p)$ returns true if and only if $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with edge list $E$.

results.title: The HAMPATH verifier
results.caption: Definition

If both decodings succeed, it accepts exactly when the Hamiltonian path check passes, that is, when $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on…

results.title: What the HAMPATH verifier accepts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For bit strings $x$ and $w$, the HAMPATH verifier accepts $(x, w)$ if and only if there are natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$, a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers and a list $p$ of natural numbers such that $x$ is the PATH encoding of $(s, t, n, es)$, $w$ is the witness encoding of $p$, and $p$ is a Hamiltonian path from $s$ to $t$ in the digraph on $0, \dots, n - 1$ with edge list $es$.

results.title: The verifier on an encoded instance and witness
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$, a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers and a list $p$ of natural numbers, the HAMPATH verifier applied to the PATH encoding of $(s, t, n, es)$ and the witness encoding of $p$ returns the same boolean as the Hamiltonian path check on $n$, $es$, $s$, $t$ and $p$.

results.title: Instances that do not decode are rejected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the PATH instance decoder fails on a bit string $x$, then for every bit string $w$ the HAMPATH verifier rejects $(x, w)$, that is, returns false.

results.title: Witnesses that do not decode are rejected
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the witness decoder fails on a bit string $w$, then for every bit string $x$ the HAMPATH verifier rejects $(x, w)$, that is, returns false.

results.title: Length of an encoded PATH instance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$ and every edge list $E$, the encoding of the PATH instance $(s, t, n, E)$ has length $s + t + n + 3 + \ell$, where $\ell$ is the length of the bit encoding of the edge list $E$.

results.title: HAMPATH is verified with quadratic-size witnesses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit string $x$, $x$ is a yes-instance of HAMPATH if and only if there is a bit string $w$ of length at most $(|x| + 1)^2$ such that the HAMPATH verifier accepts $(x, w)$.

results.title: One step of the HAMPATH walk
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given natural numbers $s$ and $n$, an edge list $E$, a count $c$ of vertices already seen, the previous vertex $b$, the current vertex $a$ and the list $q$ of remaining vertices, the step check is true exactly when $a < n$, $a$ does not occur in $q$, and either $c = 0$ and $a = s$, or $c \neq 0$ and $(b, a) \in E$.

results.title: The machine's walk is the check
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $s$, $t$, $n$, every edge list $E$ and every list $p$ of natural numbers, the walk over $p$ started with count $0$ and previous vertex $0$ returns the same Boolean value as the Hamiltonian path check on $(n, E, s, t, p)$.

results.title: Tops of distinct diamonds are at least $3m + 2$ apart
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the vertex numbering of the Hamiltonian path construction with $m$ clauses, where the top of diamond $i$ is the vertex $T(i) = m + i(3m + 2)$, any two indices $i \ne i'$ satisfy $T(i) + 3m + 2 \le T(i')$ or $T(i') + 3m + 2 \le T(i)$.

results.title: In-neighbours of a row vertex in Sipser's graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula with $m$ clauses, and write $T_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ and $R_{i,l} = T_i + 1 + l$. results.title: The frame of a diamond
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$ (the number of clauses) and $i$, write $t_i = m + i(3m + 2)$ for the top of diamond $i$ and $r_{i,l} = t_i + 1 + l$ for its row vertex $l$. results.title: Removing duplicates by insertion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $l$ of natural numbers, folding $l$ from the right into the empty list, prepending each element unless it is already present, gives $l$ with duplicates removed: each element is kept at its last occurrence in $l$, in order.

results.title: Length bound for the bit encoding of an edge list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B$ be a natural number and $E$ a list of pairs of natural numbers such that every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ has $u \le B$ and $v \le B$. Then the bit encoding of $E$, which writes each pair $(u, v)$ as $u$ ones, a zero, $v$ ones and a zero, has length at most $|E| \cdot (2B + 2)$, where $|E|$ is the length of $E$.

results.title: Each clause is picked up by exactly one row

results.title: The first $t$ diamonds occupy consecutive vertices

results.title: HAMPATH on an encoded instance

results.title: SAT ≤ HAMPATH preserves membership
